title: Saint Mary Magdalene (22 July)

cards: Mary Magdalene, the repentant prostitute: that's the woman in a great many paintings, films and sermons, going back centuries. The Gospels never say it. Not once.

What they do say about her is far more interesting, and in 2016 the Church did something about it. Pope Francis raised her day, the twenty-second of July, from a memorial to a feast, the same rank as the apostles.
And the Vatican's decree gave her an old title: apostle of the apostles.

teach.b: Here's what the Gospels actually say. Luke names her among the women who traveled with Jesus and supported his work from their own means, and says seven devils had gone out of her: some serious affliction, healed.

teach.h: AT THE CROSS, AT THE TOMB.
teach.b: Matthew, Mark and John name her at the cross, after the other disciples had scattered. And all four put her at the empty tomb on Easter morning.
In John she's alone in the garden, weeping, and mistakes the risen Jesus for the gardener until he says one word: her name, Mary. Then he sends her. Go to my brethren.

teach.h: SENT: I HAVE SEEN THE LORD.
teach.b: And John says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Mary Magdalen cometh, and telleth the disciples: I have seen the Lord, and these things he said to me."
In John, the first person sent to announce the resurrection is a woman, and the people she's sent to are the apostles. That's where the title comes from: apostle means one who is sent.
So where did the other story come from? In 591, in a homily, Pope Gregory the Great treated Mary Magdalene, the unnamed sinful woman who anoints Jesus in Luke, and Mary of Bethany as one person.
That reading shaped Western art and preaching for centuries. The Eastern churches kept them as three women.

After the Second Vatican Council, the Roman calendar quietly separated them again, and the Gospel for her day became the garden in John. Thomas Aquinas, long before, had already called her apostolorum apostola.
The Church's own feast now tells her story the way the Gospels do.

how: Catholics keep the feast of Saint Mary Magdalene on 22 July, raised from a memorial in 2016; the Gospel at Mass is John's account of her meeting the risen Jesus in the garden and being sent to the disciples.

games.q: you're in the garden, weeping at the empty tomb. a man you take for the gardener speaks to you. what makes you recognize him?
games.why: he says one word: Mary. then he sends her to the brethren, and she goes: I have seen the Lord.

practice: Think back over the last week and find one piece of genuinely good news, yours or someone else's: a recovery, a kindness, a baby, a reconciliation, a small win.
Hold it a moment, let yourself feel it, and picture who would be glad to hear it. If you pray, you can give thanks for it first.

wordCard.voice: apostolorum apostola. Latin for apostle of the apostles, the old title for Mary Magdalene, sent first from the garden to announce the resurrection. Today's word.
